name: Moodular Arithmetic
description: As behooves any intelligent schoolboy, Kevin Sun is studying psycowlogy, cowculus, and cryptcowgraphy at the Bovinia State University (BGU) under Farmer Ivan. During his Mathematics of Olympiads (MoO) class, Kevin was confronted with a weird functional equation and needs your help. For two fixed integers k and p , where p is an odd prime number, the functional equation states that for some function . (This equation should hold for any integer x in the range 0 to p - 1 , inclusive.) It turns out that f can actually be many different functions. Instead of finding a solution, Kevin wants you to count the number of distinct functions f that satisfy this equation. Since the answer may be very large, you should print your result modulo 10 9 + 7 .
input_specification: The input consists of two space-separated integers p and k ( 3 ≤ p ≤ 1 000 000 , 0 ≤ k ≤ p - 1 ) on a single line. It is guaranteed that p is an odd prime number.
output_specification: Print a single integer, the number of distinct functions f modulo 10 9 + 7 .
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 603B — Moodular Arithmetic [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
